prerequisites: Successful completion of the modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.
Recommended: knowledge in mathematics and technical mechanics, as taught in basic mechanical engineering lectures.
Recommended: knowledge from "Fundamentals of Manufacturing Technology" and materials science.

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have the methodological foundations for calculating and simulating technical systems in forming, joining, and component testing technology using the software tool "LS-Dyna".
They know the relationships between experiment, characteristic value determination, and simulation, as well as relevant application examples.
They are able to independently implement simple tasks using LS-Dyna.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the basic functionality of LS-Dyna and the structure of the user interface (e.g., LS-PrePost)
In-depth treatment of different aspects of the software relevant to forming technology
Simulative application examples (forming production of a profile from sheet metal) validated by experiments
Transfer of know-how to joining technology and component testing
Experimental determination of characteristic values (e.g., tensile specimens, LWF-KS-2 specimens) in the laboratory
Creation of input parameters for the simulation part
Construction of a real component-like model (e.g., a profile/sill)
Comparison of simulation results with reality using a sample crash test in a laboratory setting
assessment_rules: The allocation of credit points is subject to passing the module examination. The examination can be a 120-minute written exam or a 30-45 minute oral exam.
